items.item_text: Bachelors or four (4) years of experience in a directly related field.
Masters degree (MHA, MBA, MPH, Nursing, or related discipline) preferred.
High School Diploma or General Education Development (GED) required.
Minimum ten (10) years of progressive leadership experience in healthcare operations, including emergency department or other 24/7 acute care environments.
Demonstrated experience leading multi site or system level clinical operations in a complex health system.
National Strategy & System Design
Develops and leads a systemwide strategy for emergency department services aligned with organizational priorities, access goals, and care delivery transformation.
Defines the future state operating model for EDs and front door alternatives, including integration with inpatient, ambulatory, and virtual care.
Serves as a thought leader on industry trends, benchmarks, and best practices related to emergency services and acute access.
Operational Performance & Standardization
Establishes enterprise standards, policies, and performance expectations for emergency departments operations.
Partners with regions and medical centers to improve patient flow, throughput, length of stay, left without being seen rates, and patient experience.
Oversees systemwide monitoring of quality, safety, access, and operational metrics for ED services.
Identifies variation in performance and leads the development of scalable best practices to drive consistent, high reliability operations.
Quality, Safety, and Regulatory Readiness
Ensures alignment with federal, state, and accreditation requirements
Supports readiness for regulatory surveys, audits, and trauma designation requirements in partnership with quality and compliance teams.
Promotes a culture of patient and workforce safety, continuous learning, and just culture across all emergency settings.
Integration Across the Continuum
Works closely with hospital operations, medical groups, and care delivery leaders to design and implement alternatives to the emergency department, including observation and care at home models.
Partners with EMS, transfer center, and bed management leaders to ensure right patient, right time, right location, and right level of care.
Strengthens coordination between EDs, inpatient units, specialty services, and ambulatory partners to improve transitions of care.
Leadership & Change Management
Leads complex, cross functional initiatives without direct authority, influencing regional and local leaders through governance and partnership.
Acts as a change agent to support operational redesign in high acuity, high complexity environments.
Coaches and mentors emerging leaders and supports leadership development across ED operations.
Strong knowledge of emergency services operations, patient flow, regulatory requirements, and quality improvement.
Proven ability to lead large scale operational change through influence and partnership.
